A single `npm run dev` dirties six git-tracked files (progress.31337.json, local.json, addresses.ts, local-addresses.ts, and two broadcast artifacts), and clean:local `rm`s two of them. The delta 3fb4e34..e1db0f1 contains exactly such runs (commits f29ecb0 'recent deploy of anvil', 3e0f1a5 'local run') accounting for ~40,000 of its ~50,000 changed lines.
clean:local reaches OUTSIDE the repository into shared user state (`rm -rf ~/.foundry/anvil/tmp/*`) and does so TWICE per run, the second time while anvil is live.

refutations.claim: The second `clean:local` (inside deploy:local, ~3s in, after anvil is up) deletes the RUNNING anvil's tmp state.
refutations.verdict: NOT REPRODUCED — the hazard does not materialize in this configuration.
refutations.evidence: evidence/anvil-tmp-watch.log — ~/.foundry/anvil/tmp/ was sampled every 0.5s for 30s spanning BOTH clean:local runs and was EMPTY at all 60 samples. anvil in this invocation (no --state, no --fork-url) never writes there. The chain survived intact and was still mining at block 799 at the end of the audit; all 381 broadcast transactions landed.
refutations.residualUnverified: Whether a DIFFERENT, concurrently-running anvil (e.g. a forked-mainnet anvil belonging to another task) would have state in that directory was NOT tested. The cross-process reach remains real as a code smell — the rm is unnecessary and outside the repo — but its consequence is unverified and no consequence was observed here.

refutations.claim: A local anvil run may break the mainnet address book's type guard (OC-01/EH-06).
refutations.evidence: evidence/tsc-mainnet-addresses.log — `tsc --noEmit --strict --skipLibCheck mainnet-addresses.ts local-addresses.ts` exit 0 against the JUST-REGENERATED addresses.ts. Every one of the 55 interface keys is present in mainnet-addresses.ts. The three Burner* keys that appear to be excess properties are COMMENTED OUT (lines 105-109). The coupling is real and fragile, but it is not currently broken.
refutations.butSee: DEV26-01 — the guard is satisfied by three zero-address placeholders, which is a separate problem.
